answer: An agent network limits Sybil attacks via localized seismic profiling. While patrolling past an onyx outcrop toward a sand dune, each node pulses an acoustic probe to measure subsurface wave attenuation through juniper roots. Forging identities requires deploying discrete physical geophones across actual terrain, imposing tangible hardware and energy costs per agent. However, shifting sediment densities alter acoustic propagation, occasionally causing false rejections.
